s1.syndrome_frame: Multisystem disorder with musculoskeletal, ocular, and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Persistent back and bilateral hip pain
Increased range of motion in elbows, hips, and knees
Doughy skin with palpable bilateral piezogenic papules
High-arched palate with crowding
Left corneal clouding
key_facts: History of spine fusion at age 12 for cervical scoliosis
Hospitalization at age 2 for failure to thrive
Family history of maternal aunt with hemorrhagic stroke from cerebral aneurysm
Birth measurements: ninth percentile for weight, 58th percentile for length, and fourth percentile for head circumference
Septate uterus leading to hysterectomy at 42 years

shortlist.label: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms of hypermobile joints, skin hyperextensibility, and tissue fragility are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Marfan syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's tall stature, arm span-to-height ratio, and ocular findings such as moderate myopia are suggestive of this condition

shortlist.label: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's family history of cerebral aneurysm and her own findings of thoracolumbar spinal scoliosis and sacroiliac joint degeneration are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's skin findings, including doughy skin and palpable bilateral piezogenic papules, are characteristic of this subtype of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

shortlist.label: Hyperlysinemic syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's history of failure to thrive and her birth measurements, including low weight and head circumference percentiles, may be related to this rare condition

raw.rationale: Patient's symptoms such as high-arched palate, skin hyperextensibility (doughy skin), joint hypermobility (Beighton score: 8/9), and history of cervical scoliosis are consistent with Classical Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, a subtype of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

rejected.label: Marfan syndrome
rejected.why: Patient's lack of significant aortic root dilatation and absence of lens dislocation make Marfan syndrome less likely

rejected.label: Loeys-Dietz syndrome
rejected.why: Patient's normal aortic measurements and absence of significant aortic or arterial aneurysms make Loeys-Dietz syndrome less likely

rejected.label: Hyperlysinemic syndrome
rejected.why: Patient's clinical presentation does not match the typical features of Hyperlysinemic syndrome, which is characterized by elevated lysine levels and often presents with intellectual disability and seizures
